primitives.name: Discriminandum Equivalence Class
primitives.verbatim_quote: To define exactly, however, the expected discriminandum in such a case, we must discover (a) just what other light waves can be interchanged for the original one without causing such disruption, and (b) just what range of other waves cannot be thus substituted.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'λ': 'wavelength in meters', 'Δλ': 'wavelength difference in meters', 'B(λ)': 'behavioral response function'}
primitives.assumptions: Light wavelengths form an ordered set under perceptual indistinguishability; behavioral responses are deterministic within equivalence classes.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When Δλ exceeds intrinsic discriminability threshold, B(λ) exhibits discontinuity.

layer2.mapping: Equivalence class of λ under B(λ) is isomorphic to a partition of sensory space in GSI's probabilistic model.
layer2.telemetry: Observable behavioral disruption upon stimulus substitution.

primitives.name: Intrinsic Discrimination Ordering
primitives.verbatim_quote: We must know what these intrinsic orders are for the specific case of color and for the specific species of animal.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'O(λ₁, λ₂)': 'order relation between wavelengths', 'D(λ₁, λ₂)': 'discriminability distance'}
primitives.assumptions: Intrinsic ordering defines a partial order on wavelength space; D(λ₁, λ₂) is symmetric and reflexive.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When D(λ₁, λ₂) approaches zero, O(λ₁, λ₂) becomes undefined.

layer2.mapping: Ordering kernel derived from empirical color-pyramid data; used in GSE to compute transition probabilities.

primitives.name: Behavioral Disruption Manifold
primitives.verbatim_quote: If on any occasion this specific color fails to be present, the given behavior will, that is, by hypothesis, show disruption; it will give way to some other behavior on the immediately subsequent occasions.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'M(λ₀)': 'manifold of behaviors at reference wavelength', "M'(λ₁)": 'manifold of alternative behaviors at perturbed wavelength'}
primitives.assumptions: Manifolds are smooth except at points of discontinuity; disruption occurs when λ₁ ∉ λ₀'s equivalence class.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Discontinuity occurs when M(λ₀) ≠ M'(λ₁) for λ₁ ∈ Δλ.

layer2.mapping: Manifold mismatch in GSE corresponds to discriminandum failure in GSI's Bayesian update.
layer2.telemetry: Temporal sequence of behavioral shifts post-stimulus change.

This leads to the formalization of an equivalence class of wavelengths that produce indistinguishable behavioral outcomes. The intrinsic ordering of these classes forms a kernel that maps to the structure of the color-pyramid, enabling probabilistic modeling of sensory discrimination. When a stimulus deviates beyond the equivalence class, a behavioral disruption manifold is triggered, indicating a failure mode in the discriminandum. The mathematical framework thus unifies perception, cognition, and action through ordered sets and topological manifolds. The color-pyramid serves as a concrete instantiation of this abstract structure, providing empirical grounding for both Bayesian inference in GSI and state-transition logic in GSE.
